title: Blood Bank — Emergency Release Requested

transcript.speaker: Lena Park
transcript.text: ED Medical Director, this is Lena Park from Blood Bank. We have a trauma patient arriving from ambulance bay 2. No history is available. The lab system is down, so we can’t pull the prior antibody screen or ABO type. I have 14 units of O-negative on hand and I need to initiate an emergency release. Can you confirm we follow the downtime blood protocol?

transcript.speaker: Dr. Elaine Whitfield
transcript.text: Lena, confirm you’ve activated the emergency release form and are using the second-person check. I’ll sign the release now. Is the patient stable enough for immediate transfusion?

transcript.speaker: Lena Park
transcript.text: Yes, the patient is in hypovolemic shock, Glasgow 7, intubated. We’re preparing to infuse. The second nurse is at the bedside now.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Elaine Whitfield
transcript.text: Good. Sign the emergency release, and document the second check on the paper record. I’ll ensure the EHR downtime form is updated in the HCC.

instructorNote: This inject tests the blood bank’s adherence to the downtime protocol and the ED’s ability to authorize emergency release under paper-based documentation. Watch for the second-person check and proper use of the paper record.
